title: Maymana protest over detention of Uzbek Taliban commander Makhdoom Alam
scope: Reported public demonstration over detention/release of Makhdoom Alam, followed by or intertwined with armed disputes among Taliban factions. Whether public protest, armed pressure, and subsequent clashes are one episode remains unresolved.
participants_original: The National, Khaama, Hasht and DW use “hundreds”/“mass”; Etilaatroz says “dozens.” No precise attendance count is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: DW and multiple other reports describe hundreds; Etilaatroz says dozens. Qualitative estimates conflict and participant boundaries relative to armed Taliban actors are unclear, so retain the threshold decision for human review.

title.summary: Etilaatroz and DW Dari identify the action as a Maimana/Faryab protest over Makhdoom Alam’s detention.

start_date.summary: Both Dari reports date the public action to Thursday 13 Jan.; the Jan. 16 Hasht report’s relative “four days ago” still implies Jan. 12 and remains unreconciled.

end_date.summary: Etilaatroz does not give a physical closing date. DW describes a Friday call to resume protest at Eidgah Mosque and a dispersal, but does not establish whether this was a continuation or separate gathering.

location.summary: Both reports locate the action in Maimana, Faryab; DW locates the later Friday attempted restart at Eidgah Mosque.

scope.summary: Etilaatroz describes a street protest and tent outside the governor’s office. DW says protest turned violent and separately reports a Friday attempted restart/dispersal; relationship between forms/sequences remains open.

demands.summary: Etilaatroz says protesters demanded that the central Taliban government release Alam; DW corroborates the detention issue and demand but does not supply separate turnout/organization facts.

participants.summary: Etilaatroz says “dozens”; DW says “hundreds.” Neither provides a precise count; the estimates conflict qualitatively.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: DW and earlier reports characterize the main gathering as hundreds, while Etilaatroz reports dozens; no exact count or clear boundary between protesters and armed actors is available. Leave the ≥50 judgment for review.

state_response.summary: DW reports governor’s-office guards fired at protesters according to protesters, cites clashes/casualties, and says Taliban forces dispersed a Friday attempted restart. These reports are saved for review; no response code is assigned here.

protester_violence.summary: DW says the protest turned violent but does not specify what protesters did; the one Taliban officer killed and four protester injuries are source claims, not a coder inference of protester violence.

notes: The strongest direct reports place the protest on Jan. 13 and describe demand to release the detained commander and ethnic representation grievances. One later report, published Jan. 16, says “four days ago” (approximately Jan. 12). The protest later overlaps with intra-Taliban armed confrontation; do not treat deaths or violence in those clashes as state response at a protest. Additional Dari reports date the street protest to 13 Jan.; Etilaatroz says dozens and describes a tent outside the governor’s office, while DW says hundreds and reports an ensuing violent clash, alleged guard fire, casualties and a separately described Jan. 14 attempted restart/dispersal. No armed casualty is assigned as a state response, and no protester-violence code is inferred; onset, sequence, end and response remain for review.
open_questions: Reconcile Jan. 12/13 start dating; determine whether protest met the public assembly/state-policy criteria separately from armed Taliban activity; identify physical end, organizer, exact turnout and protester violence.
Clarify whether the Jan. 14 Eidgah assembly/dispersal was an actual second public gathering, a continuation, or only an attempted restart; attendance is unknown.

Review DW’s claims of guard firing, one Taliban officer killed and four protesters injured for actor/sequence attribution; do not infer protester violence or assign armed-conflict casualties without linkage.
Assess whether DW, Etilaatroz and earlier outlets provide independent reporting or overlapping local-source accounts.

location.summary: CIR locates the public action in Kabul.

scope.summary: The chronology does not provide enough detail to connect this to another reported protest.

demands.summary: Reviewed text identifies the arrest as preceding context but does not clearly state the protesters’ demand.

participants.summary: No participant count is reported in the reviewed chronology.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or explicit threshold evidence.

state_response.summary: No particular response to this gathering was established.

protester_violence.summary: No violence finding established for this specific action.

title: Kabul women’s protest against restrictions on movement and dress
scope: Public women’s demonstration reported by VOA Deewa and included in a retrospective chronology; likely the same gathering across reports, not independently counted as separate events.

title.summary: VOA Deewa and CIR describe a public Kabul demonstration by women against restrictions.

start_date.summary: VOA Deewa says Jan. 11; CIR chronology lists Jan. 11.

location.summary: Both sources locate the reported action in Kabul.

scope.summary: Likely same Jan. 11 action; no attendance/organizer record proves matching identity.

demands.summary: VOA reports opposition to mahram travel restrictions and compulsory hijab; banners included jobs, education, freedom.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or explicit evidence of at least 50.

state_response.summary: VOA says Taliban fighters later stopped the demonstrators; treatment as crowd dispersal remains a coding question. Other response dimensions unknown.

protester_violence.summary: Article does not provide a clear finding on protester violence.

notes: VOA Deewa describes women protesting restrictions requiring a male guardian for travel and compulsory hijab; banners also referred to jobs, education and freedom. The report says Taliban fighters later stopped the protest. No count is reported. The correspondence with CIR’s Jan. 11 public Kabul action is plausible but not independently confirmed.
open_questions: Find turnout and confirm reports identify the same action; clarify whether Taliban fighters stopping marchers constitutes coded crowd dispersal under the codebook; determine closing time.

title: Women demonstrate in Kabul for government jobs and equal representation
scope: Public demonstration reported in an IANS article published Jan. 13; date is inferred from its “Wednesday” reference to Jan. 12. It may relate to the broader month’s women-led actions but is not shown to be the Jan. 11 or Jan. 13 action.
participants_original: “Dozens of women” (original qualitative estimate); exact number not given.

title.summary: Times of India/IANS report describes women demanding jobs and equal representation.

start_date.summary: Article published Jan. 13 describes a Wednesday protest, corresponding to Jan. 12.

location.summary: Article locates the action in Kabul.

scope.summary: One public demonstration is reported; relation to separate women’s actions is unresolved.

demands.summary: Reported demands are government jobs and equal representation.

participants.summary: Report says “dozens of women”; no exact count or range is given.

state_response.summary: No particular response dimensions established in this report.

protester_violence.summary: No violence finding established for the gathering.

notes: Times of India/IANS reports that dozens of women protested for government jobs and equal representation. Its report cites TOLO; do not count later TOLO search leads as independent corroboration.
open_questions: Clarify exact attendance, whether “dozens” was below or above 50, exact event date, organizer and relation to other Kabul demonstrations.

title: Outdoor demonstration in Bamiyan against Oslo meeting and detention of women activists
scope: Public/outdoor demonstration listed in a retrospective chronology, with demands concerning release of Kabul women protesters and Alia Azizi and opposition to the Oslo meeting. Exact state target and event scope need confirmation.

demands.summary: Reported issues include opposition to the Oslo meeting and release of Kabul protesters/Alia Azizi; whether all are direct demands to Afghanistan’s government needs review.

notes: CIR identifies an outdoor protest but gives no size. Plural women-led actions do not establish the >=50 threshold.
open_questions: Confirm turnout, exact location, organizer, whether the Oslo-related demand is aimed at domestic Taliban policy/actors, and whether this is a separate action.

organizer: Women activists (not named as an organization)

start_date.summary: The article is dated 24 Jan. 2022 and dates the protest to that day.

location.summary: The article places the action in Daykundi Province.

scope.summary: The source says the protest occurred indoors; the exact venue and public access are unspecified.

demands.summary: A participant called for proper aid management and for aid workers to monitor distribution; the report does not identify a responsible government body.

participants.summary: No attendance figure or estimate is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence establishes 50 or more participants.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is reported.

notes: This is a provisional event lead only. The single article reports an indoor action and gives no attendance, exact venue, public-access status or clear domestic state target. Do not code as qualifying without evidence for the 50-person and government-target criteria.
open_questions: Was this gathering open to the public or a private meeting?
Did it reach at least 50 participants?
Which domestic government actor or policy was the demand aimed at?
Were aid workers understood to act for the state or for independent organizations?
Was there any event-specific state response?

title: Kabul rally reported over the violent deaths of two women
scope: A retrospective EUAA report names a January rally over the violent death of two women in Kabul. It does not give an exact date, attendance, specific demand, event identity or state response in the reviewed passage.

title.summary: EUAA separately identifies a rally over the violent death of two women in Kabul during Jan. 2022.

start_date.summary: The reviewed EUAA passage gives the month but no rally date.

location.summary: EUAA places the rally in Kabul.

scope.summary: The report’s women’s-assembly section mentions the rally; its reviewed text does not establish turnout or exact event identity.

demands.summary: The report names the topic but does not state the rally’s explicit demand or target in the reviewed passage.

participants.summary: No attendance is provided in the reviewed passage.

state_response.summary: The report discusses women’s protests generally, but no response is assigned to this rally.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific violence finding is supplied.

notes: Retrospective lead only. EUAA cites a TOLO report dated 16 Jan. titled “Kabul Protest Spotlights Recent Killing of 2 Women”; that TOLO item is on the same origin as a blocked target already recorded in this unit and was not retried. This may overlap with excluded Jan. 16 Kabul demonstrations (E008 vs X008); do not count as a separate event without identity/turnout evidence.
open_questions: Was this the Jan. 16 protest covered by sources for the approximately 20–25 participant demonstration, or a distinct rally?
What was the exact action date and explicit demand/target?
Was attendance at least 50?
What was the event-specific state response?

title: Kabul women’s protest for release of Afghanistan’s frozen funds
scope: The opened EUAA report discusses Jan./Feb. Kabul protests over frozen funds and cites a Khaama article dated 26 Jan. with a title describing Afghan women protesting for release of frozen funds. The exact contemporary article is blocked; its event details, publicness, attendance and state target are unverified.
organizer: Unknown; the EUAA citation/title refers to women protesters but no organizer is established in the reviewed text.

title.summary: The opened EUAA bibliography cites the Khaama report title “Afghan women protest for release of Afghanistan’s frozen funds”; the exact contemporary article was not read.

start_date.summary: EUAA bibliographic entry dates the cited Khaama report to 26 Jan. 2022; the article body date was not independently verified.

location.summary: EUAA’s reviewed women’s-assembly section identifies Jan./Feb. frozen-funds protests in Kabul and cites a Jan. 26 Khaama report, but exact event-to-entry linkage is indirect.

scope.summary: Retrospective EUAA report and article title provide a frozen-funds protest lead; direct article facts are unavailable due exact-URL HTTP 403.

demands.summary: The topic is frozen funds; the precise demand and target for this specific event are not established by the reviewed secondary passage.

participants.summary: No attendance is stated in reviewed EUAA passages, and the direct Khaama body was not read.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No admissible event-specific evidence establishes at least 50 participants; search snippets were not used.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is established in reviewed materials.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific protester violence finding is established.

notes: Provisional lead from a retrospective bibliography. Direct Khaama page returned HTTP 403 and is under an exact-URL hold (R030); no alternate outlet or host was used to obtain the same reported action. No attendance or target facts are adopted from search snippets. It is unclear whether the demand targeted Afghanistan’s state or foreign authorities, and whether the referenced date/location form one distinct action.
open_questions: Does the Khaama citation correspond to the Kabul Jan. 26 frozen-assets protest described in EUAA’s section?
Was the action a public gathering and did it reach 50 people?
What specific state or government policy was the demand directed at, and does the target fit the codebook?
Was the action aligned with and supporting the interim government, and how does that affect target classification?
What was event-specific state response and were there protester-violence reports?
